quote: return [];  // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Corrupt or unreadable saved data is silently treated as empty, and the next save overwrites it
evidence: Driven: localStorage 'recipes' = '{bad', reload. The list shows the empty state and the status is empty, so app.js does not tell the user (the comment is wrong; app.js never checks why loadRecipes returned []). Adding one recipe then wrote only the new recipe to storage. loadRecipes also drops records with no string name (store.js:7) with no notice.
failing_case: One bad byte in the saved JSON, or one record with no name, makes the page open as 'No recipes yet'. The user adds a recipe; saveRecipes replaces the whole stored value and the original recipes are gone for good.
remediation: Have loadRecipes return a result that says what happened ({list, error}). On a parse failure, keep the raw string under a backup key before any write, show a status message, and do not overwrite until the user chooses.

title: Each tab keeps its own copy of the list and the last save overwrites the other tab's recipes
evidence: Driven: two pages on the same origin, both loaded empty. Tab A saved 'FromA', then tab B saved 'FromB'. Storage held only [FromB]. The app never re-reads storage before a write and has no 'storage' event listener.
failing_case: The user keeps the app open in two tabs (or a restored session), adds a recipe in each. The first tab's recipe is erased from storage with a 'Saved' message.
remediation: Re-read storage (loadRecipes) inside each mutation before pushing or filtering, and listen to the window 'storage' event to re-render when another tab writes.

title: Exponent input in the number field is saved as the wrong minutes
evidence: Driven: typing 1e2 in the Minutes field (valid for type=number, min=1 max=600) saved 'Soup 1 min' with status 'Total cooking time: 1 minutes.' parseInt stops at the 'e'.
failing_case: User enters 1e2 (100) and is shown a saved recipe of 1 minute. No error is shown.
remediation: Use e.target.elements.minutes.valueAsNumber (or Number(value)) and require Number.isInteger(minutes) && minutes >= 1 && minutes <= 600 so the script check matches the markup.

title: Delete shows "Deleted" even when the save failed; the recipe returns on reload
evidence: Driven in Chromium. With localStorage.setItem throwing, clicking Delete and confirming left the status at 'Deleted “A”.' The add handler (app.js:24-25) checks saveRecipes' return value; the delete handler (app.js:35-36) ignores it.
failing_case: Storage is full or blocked. User deletes 'A' and confirms. The status announces 'Deleted “A”.' and the list drops it. On reload the stored list still holds 'A'. A failure is reported as success.
remediation: Use the return value of saveRecipes in the delete handler: on false, show the same kind of failure message as the add handler and say the deletion lasts only until the tab closes. Share one helper between add and delete.

title: Deleting a recipe rebuilds the list and drops keyboard focus to the page body
evidence: Driven: after confirming Delete on the first row, document.activeElement was BODY. render() replaces the whole list via innerHTML, destroying the focused button. The status is announced, but the focus position is lost (WCAG 2.4.3 focus order).
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs to the second recipe's Delete button and deletes it. Focus falls to the top of the page, so they must tab through the form again to reach the next Delete.
remediation: After render in the delete handler, move focus to the next row's Delete button, or the previous one, or the Name input when the list is empty.

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: Loaded records are only checked for a name; a record without id or minutes shows NaN, poisons the total and crashes Delete
evidence: Driven with stored [{name:'Old'},{id:7,name:'Num',minutes:10}]. The list shows 'Old NaN min'. Clicking Delete on it throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')' at app.js:33/36, because the data-id 'undefined' matches no record and r is undefined (the comment at app.js:14 says that cannot happen). With [{id:'1',...},{id:'2',name:'NoMin'}], adding a recipe set the status to 'Total cooking time: NaN minutes.' A numeric id (7) never matches the string dataset.id either, so that record cannot be deleted.
failing_case: Any record saved by an earlier version with no id or minutes, or with a numeric id. The list renders NaN min, every later save message reports a NaN total, and Delete on that row throws and does nothing, so the record can't be removed.
remediation: Normalise each record once at load: String(id) or a new id, Number(minutes) required to be finite and > 0, drop or repair the rest and count what was dropped. Guard the delete handler against a missing record.
